restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages m(a), m(b) of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 (zero state, rate 136, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5, full 256-bit digest). m(u) places the point u (lanes u0..u3) in lanes 1, 11, 6 = u0^K1, u1^K11, u0^u1^K6 and lanes 9, 14, 4 = u2^K9, u3^K14, u2^u3^K4, the other lanes 0..15 fixed constants K (proof.md Section 2); m is injective. F(u) = digest of m(u) xor a fixed mask PD; F(a) = F(b) with a != b is an ordinary collision. Column sums of the message lanes are constant and the chi neighbors of the six variable lanes after round-0 theta, rho and pi are all-zero or all-one annihilating constants, so round 0 (leaving 14 of 25 output lanes constant) and round-1 theta are affine in u with only 1,088 distinct affine forms (an annihilating Guo-Liu-Song 2016 linear structure, building on bc3e3eef).

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on F with 256 walks per step, as in entries 2d74a370 and bc3e3eef: DP = planes 142..255 zero (H = 114), cap 17 x 2^114 steps, at most 21,000 trails and a table of 21,000 words, Tb = 67878312 x 2^94 steps, a prefilter-hit counter that aborts the attempt at hit HMAX + 1 (HMAX = floor(Tb (1 + 2^-20)/2^8) + 1 + Lc), one replay with the selected-round permutation (proof.md Section 4).

One step of 256 walks is a generated bit-sliced straight line of 27,391 register operations (20,307 XOR, 3,982 AND, 2,674 OR, 428 NOT; no loads or stores): lazy per-row theta, 1-round lookahead per-row complement pairs (s, f) with NOT reuse across rows, dead-code elimination, last-use allocation (building on jungjipdo's 67f781f8 and bc3e3eef, our generator gen.c, Appendix B). Executed and compared with a plain six-round implementation: 2,048 and 16,384 chained evaluations, 0 mismatches (Section 3.7).

Cost model collision-frontier-v5, unit 1626: N = Tb x 27,411 + (2 x 1661 + 19) x Lc + R + PRE = 38074419192659037121819726591419275724248 word operations, every loop-control, test and handler operation counted, at most HMAX + 1 prefilter hits at 116 each in every execution, PRE = 33 x 2^32 + 32 x 2^10 for the selection run gen 32, replay at one unit per permutation call plus 35 (Section 4); time_log2 = 124.13884 = log2(N/1626) rounded up, integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12413883 < N^100000 <= 1626^100000 2^12413884 (Appendix A).

Machine conventions H_reg and H_code (role supporting; the cost model fixes neither; Section 3.5): H_reg, a declared file of 2,192 registers of 256 bits, the same convention as 67f781f8 and bc3e3eef, its 70,144 bytes counted as memory, an operation on registers costing one word operation, every load and store of the other code charged; H_code, a code-memory charging rule of 5 bytes per straight-line instruction and 32 bytes per instruction of other code, the time ledger counting one word operation per straight-line instruction. Priced alternatives in Section 8 (1,024 registers 124.561, 512 registers 124.766, 256 registers 124.915, 64 registers 125.078, 32-byte code about 124.76).

Memory at most 1,036,870 bytes <= 2^20 (registers, code, table, walk state, scratch, constants; Section 6); the selection run gen 32 runs before the search (phases do not overlap): gen.c declares 817,732 bytes of static data and BSS (image 838,212) and gen 32 completes under an address-space limit of 2^20 bytes; bound used 1,007,935 with a 32,768-byte stack reserve and its 136,955-byte output, measured resident peak at most 602,112 bytes; so memory_log2_bytes = 20 and the score is 124.13884. The declared Python experiments are reduced-width evidence, not the attack.

Success at least 0.39 for one attempt over the fresh word rho, under the score-critical premise H_rand (F behaves as a random function on the evaluated points), with failure terms for cut trails, table limit (proved by exact Binomial stochastic domination via lazy sampling), self-coincidence, starts and key matches, and the hit-counter abort F5 < 2^-1000, proved by a Chernoff bound (Section 5). Preprocessing: the constant-selection run gen 32 (32 algebraic constant sets, the best rebuilt), charged 33 x 2^32 + 32 x 2^10 operations, preprocessing_log2 27. No advice. No full-scale run and no full collision is claimed.

heuristics.statement: F(u) = SHA3-256-r6(m(u)) xor PD, with the annihilating linear-structure message embedding m of proof.md Section 2, behaves as a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values on the points the search evaluates: values at distinct inputs are independent and uniform, a fresh point is a distinguished point with probability 2^-114, and the remaining length of a trail after a coincidence is geometric with parameter 2^-114 independently of the time of the coincidence. Then the first image coincidence among e evaluations has probability at least 1 - exp(-e(e-1)/2^257), and one attempt succeeds with probability at least 0.39 after the failure terms of proof.md Section 5.
heuristics.scope: The fixed function F of proof.md Section 2 on the points of one attempt: about 1.0115 x 2^128 evaluations in 256 lockstep walks from starts rho + i, i < 21,000. Only the pair-coincidence rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate enter the bound. Nothing else is assumed: the step program, the cost, the memory and the failure terms are derived.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-executed: rho-w22 runs the whole search with the claimed straight line at width 22 (every trial must return a 22-bit partial collision; our 2,304 local trials took 17.72 steps on average against 17.94 for an ideal random function, z = -1.5); proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps and tests 22-bit agreement among 2,048 iterates (model 0.3934 per trial; our 2,304 Python trials gave 914/2,304 = 0.3967, z = +0.3). Our own C runs (proof.md Section 7.2) on the program file: pair-coincidence rates on three 32-bit windows (including the distinguished-point bits) among 2^24 images of uniform inputs, of the consecutive starts rho + i, and of chained iterates are within 1.2 percent of the random value (sd 0.55 percent); single-bit input differences show no output bias (max |z| 4.31 over 65,536 cells, mean z^2 0.9912); the proj trial at scale gives 0.3945 in 262,144 trials (z = +1.2). Extrapolated from 22- and 32-bit projections to 256-bit coincidences at 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption, not proved. The linear round 0 leaves five nonlinear rounds; a structural deviation of the collision rate at 256 bits that does not appear in 22- and 32-bit projections is not excluded. If the pair-coincidence rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, the same success costs about 0.5 log2(1/(1 - eps)) more bits (0.0073 for eps = 0.01). Both our Python proj-w256 runs (914/2,304 = 0.3967, z = +0.3) and our C run at scale (103,420/262,144 = 0.3945, z = +1.2) match the random-function model 0.3934.

heuristics.statement: Machine convention: the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 with a declared file of 2,192 registers of 256 bits (2,181 used by the straight line, 11 by the search state). An operation on register operands costs one word operation, with no load or store; every load and store of the other code is a charged word operation (proof.md Sections 3.5 and 4). The 70,144 bytes of the file are counted as memory (Section 6). The cost model fixes no register count. This is the same convention as 67f781f8 (2,304 registers) and bc3e3eef (2,192 registers), which are declared dependencies of this package.
heuristics.scope: The register file of the machine that runs the step program and the search of proof.md Section 4; it affects the time and memory ledgers only, not the success bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: a declared convention. Priced: 1,024 registers 124.561, 512 registers 124.766, 256 registers 124.915, 64 registers 125.078 (loads and stores by Belady eviction, spill.py; proof.md Section 8). Executed checks (selftest, the experiments) validate the functional output of the program with this allocation, not the cost of register access.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer requires a smaller register file the score rises by the priced amount; the success argument is unaffected. The role supporting is the role of a declared convention and does not mean the premise is small: 1,024 registers cost +0.42 bit and 256 registers +0.78 bit.

heuristics.statement: Code-memory charging convention: a declared encoding, since the cost model and the target profile fix none. The straight line is stored at 5 bytes per instruction (3-bit opcode and three 12-bit register numbers; 137,030 bytes with the prefilter); all other code is charged 32 bytes per instruction, at most 4,096 instructions (proof.md Sections 3.5 and 6). The 5-byte straight-line encoding is the one of 67f781f8 and bc3e3eef, declared dependencies of this package.
heuristics.scope: The code rows of the memory table (proof.md Section 6); it does not affect the success bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: a declared convention. Priced: 32 bytes per instruction for the straight line gives about 124.76 (coarse parameter scan, not certified; proof.md Section 8). The executed checks decode the 5-byte encoding in software to validate the function of the program.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer requires 32 bytes per instruction for the straight line the score rises to about 124.76; the success argument is unaffected. The 4,096-instruction size of the other code is a declared bound, not a measured size; the memory margin to 2^20 is 11,706 bytes, 365 instructions of 32 bytes.
